name: Consumer Portfolio Services
desc: Buys and services subprime auto loans originated by car dealers for consumers with limited credit histories.
markets: Customers are US car buyers and dealers; operates only in the United States with no known expansion plans.
rationale: Niche B2B-oriented lender with no international footprint and low consumer awareness; little reason for an F1 partnership.

name: One97 Communications (Paytm)
desc: Operates the Paytm mobile payments platform offering UPI, wallet, merchant QR and card devices, loans and insurance distribution in India.
markets: Consumers and merchants across India; Paytm has limited operations outside India and no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Highly visible Indian consumer brand that could use F1 for brand building, but customers are almost entirely domestic.

name: Robinhood Markets
desc: Runs a retail investing app offering commission-free trading of stocks, options and crypto, retirement accounts and a credit card.
markets: Mainly US retail investors; has launched products in the UK and EU, with further international expansion under way.
rationale: Strong consumer fintech brand courting younger investors; F1 could support UK and European expansion and US brand awareness.

name: Block
desc: Financial technology group behind Square merchant payments, Cash App, Afterpay buy now pay later and Tidal music streaming.
markets: Square and Cash App serve US merchants and consumers; Afterpay and Square operate in Australia, Canada, UK, Japan and Europe.

f1: Cash App is a current Formula 1 partner (Block's consumer payments brand).

name: Shift4 Payments
desc: Provides integrated payment processing and point-of-sale software to restaurants, hotels, stadiums, retailers and online businesses.
markets: Merchants in the US and Europe, expanded through acquisitions such as Finaro and Global Blue.
rationale: B2B payments firm with venue and hospitality customers, so F1 hospitality and venue links suit its sales strategy.

name: Naver
desc: Operates South Korea's leading search engine and platform for webtoons, shopping, maps, payments, cloud and AI services.
markets: Dominant in Korea; owns Webtoon, active in Japan through the LINE stake and in North America and Europe.
rationale: Large consumer brand with Webtoon and AI services growing overseas, so F1 could build global recognition beyond Korea and Japan.

name: CleanCapital
desc: Acquires, owns and operates solar, storage and other renewable energy projects and offers an online platform for investors.
markets: Invests in clean energy assets in the United States; no verified international activity.
rationale: Investor-facing B2B platform with no consumer visibility and a domestic focus, so F1 fit is weak.

desc: Operates a cryptocurrency exchange offering trading, staking, margin, futures and custody services to retail and institutional customers.
markets: Clients in the US, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions; has filed confidentially for a US IPO.
rationale: Crypto exchange already active in motorsport sponsorship; it appears as a current Formula 1 partner, so a further deal is unlikely to be new.
f1: Kraken is listed among current Formula 1 partners.

name: Wealthsimple
desc: Offers a Canadian consumer app for investing, trading, crypto, tax filing, chequing and savings accounts and managed portfolios.
markets: Clients are Canadians; no verified expansion outside Canada.
rationale: Heavily advertised consumer brand but customers are Canadian only, so F1 offers limited commercial return beyond Canadian Grand Prix exposure.

name: Zip Co
desc: Provides buy now pay later instalment credit to consumers at retailers in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.
markets: Operates in Australia, New Zealand and the US, with the US as its main growth market.
rationale: Consumer finance brand growing in the US; F1 could aid US awareness and merchant partnerships.

name: Euronet Worldwide
desc: Operates the Epay prepaid top-up, Ria money transfer and Euronet ATM and card processing businesses and the Dandelion payments network.
markets: Services in around 200 countries to banks, mobile operators, retailers and migrant remittance customers.

name: Bitmine Immersion Technologies
desc: Holds a large corporate treasury of ether, after earlier bitcoin mining work using immersion cooling technology.
markets: US-listed holding company based in Nevada; no verified customer markets or international operations.
rationale: Investor-facing treasury vehicle with little consumer brand to market, so F1 sponsorship makes little commercial sense.

name: FalconX

markets: Merchants across Mexico; no verified operations outside Mexico.

name: Forward Financing

name: IIFL Home Finance
desc: Provides home loans, loans against property and construction finance to salaried and self-employed borrowers in India.
markets: Customers across India through a branch network, mainly in smaller cities; no international operations.

name: Lendo
desc: Runs a lending marketplace connecting small businesses and digital companies with working capital and receivable-backed financing.
markets: Based in Riyadh serving Saudi businesses; no verified activity elsewhere.

desc: Sells annuities, group retirement plans and life insurance through advisers, banks and workplace channels.

name: Masan Group
desc: Vietnamese consumer and retail conglomerate owning WinMart supermarkets, Masan Consumer food brands and meat businesses, plus a Techcombank stake.
markets: Sells to Vietnamese households through supermarkets and widely advertised food brands; no verified major overseas expansion.
rationale: Heavily advertised Vietnamese consumer brands and sports sponsor; F1 could build brand prestige but customers are almost entirely domestic.

name: Checkout.com
desc: Provides card acquiring, payment processing, fraud tools and payouts to online merchants such as Netflix, eBay, Shein, Sony and Samsung.
markets: Merchants across Europe, the Americas, Middle East and Asia-Pacific, processing hundreds of billions in volume.
rationale: Rival payments brands such as Stripe, Visa and Mastercard are F1 partners; earlier research notes its past F1 sponsorship, which is not confirmed as current.

name: Great Rock Capital
desc: Asset-based lender providing senior secured loans to middle-market companies backed by inventory, receivables and equipment.
markets: Lends to US middle-market companies; no verified international activity.
rationale: B2B specialist lender with no consumer awareness, so F1 sponsorship makes little commercial sense.

name: LPL Financial
desc: Largest independent US broker-dealer supporting financial advisors with brokerage, advisory, custody, research and technology platforms.
markets: Supports more than 22,000 financial advisors serving US retail investors; no significant international operations.
rationale: Advisor-facing brand with moderate awareness and a US-only market, so F1 offers limited return.

name: Majid Al Futtaim
desc: Emirati conglomerate owning Mall of the Emirates, City Centre malls, Carrefour franchise stores, VOX Cinemas and Ski Dubai.
markets: Operates in the Middle East, Africa and Asia, with very high consumer visibility in the Gulf.
rationale: Consumer-facing group with malls, cinemas and retail across the Gulf; F1 could drive footfall, partner promotions and regional hospitality.

name: MSCI
desc: Provides investment indexes, analytics, ESG ratings and risk models used by asset managers, banks and pension funds worldwide.
markets: Clients worldwide including asset managers, banks and pension funds; flagship MSCI World and Emerging Markets indexes.
rationale: B2B data brand known in finance; F1 hospitality and technology storytelling could reach institutional clients, as other finance partners do.

name: The GEO Group
desc: Operates private prisons, immigration detention centres, rehabilitation programmes and electronic monitoring under government contracts.
markets: Contracts with US federal agencies, plus operations in Australia and South Africa.
rationale: Controversial government contractor with significant reputational sensitivity and no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship is very unlikely.

name: Waystar
desc: Provides cloud-based revenue cycle software for claims, patient payments and prior authorisation to hospitals, health systems and physician groups.
markets: Customers are US hospitals, health systems and physician groups; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B healthcare software with no consumer awareness and a US-only market, so F1 offers little return.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2024

name: DANA Indonesia
desc: Indonesian digital wallet and payments app used for QR payments, bill payments, transfers and e-commerce.
markets: Tens of millions of users in Indonesia; backed by Emtek Group and Ant Group.
rationale: Heavily promoted consumer fintech with local sports sponsorship, but its customers are in a single country.

name: Aadhar Housing Finance
desc: Provides home loans to low and middle-income and self-employed borrowers buying affordable homes through branches across India.
markets: Customers are Indian households served by several hundred branches; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic affordable housing lender with moderate regional awareness, so F1 offers little commercial return.
changed: Acquired by Blackstone in 2019 and listed in 2024

name: Bit Origin
desc: Mines bitcoin using self-owned machines and hosted facilities in the US and has announced a Dogecoin treasury strategy.
markets: Mining operations in the United States; small-cap company with no verified customer markets abroad.
rationale: Small crypto miner with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship makes little commercial sense.
changed: Pivoted from apparel retail to crypto mining

name: Blue Owl Credit Income
desc: Non-traded private credit fund managed by Blue Owl Capital, lending to mid-sized and large US companies through senior secured loans.
markets: Raises money from individual and retail investors and lends to US companies.
rationale: Financial product with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship would suit the manager at most, not the fund.

name: Fold Holdings
desc: Offers a bitcoin rewards app and cards paying cashback in bitcoin, plus gift card rewards, to US consumers.
markets: Customers are US consumers using Visa cards and a rewards app; no verified international plans.
rationale: Consumer crypto brand with modest awareness among US bitcoin users; F1 offers limited fit for a US-only audience.
changed: Listed in 2025 through a SPAC merger with FTAC Emerald

name: GoldState Music
desc: Private investment firm focused on music assets, according to Crunchbase; its holdings and clients are not confirmed.
markets: Based in West Palm Beach, Florida; investment markets and international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about its brand; as an investment vehicle for music assets it has no clear F1 rationale.

name: Lendistry
desc: Lends to small businesses, especially minority-owned and underserved ones, as a fintech and community development financial institution.
markets: Small business customers in the United States; no international operations.
rationale: Regional US small business lender with a community mission, so F1 sponsorship offers little relevance.

name: LMAX Group
desc: Operates electronic trading venues including LMAX Exchange for institutional foreign exchange, LMAX Digital for crypto and FX clearing.
markets: Institutional clients such as brokers, banks and hedge funds; regulated in the UK.
rationale: FX and trading brands such as FxPro, IC Markets and Pepperstone already sponsor F1; LMAX could use hospitality for institutional clients.

name: meutudo
desc: Brazilian fintech app offering payroll-deductible loans, credit cards and related services mainly to retirees, pensioners and public sector workers.
markets: Customers are Brazilian retirees and public sector workers; present in Brazil only.
rationale: Brazilian consumer lender with moderate local awareness; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers local exposure but market is a single country.

name: Ratio
desc: Fintech platform providing customers with financial tools, according to Crunchbase; its products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Based in San Mateo, California; customer markets and international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Little verified information on brand or scale, so no clear case for an F1 partnership.

name: Genting Berhad
desc: Malaysian conglomerate in leisure, hospitality and gaming, with resorts, casinos and cruises, plus plantations, power generation and oil and gas.
markets: Resorts in Malaysia, Singapore, the United States and the UK, plus cruise operations.
rationale: Brand-led casino and resort group; F1 could drive resort and cruise bookings in Singapore, Malaysia and Las Vegas.

name: VakifBank
desc: Turkish state-controlled bank offering retail, commercial, SME and corporate banking, insurance and asset management through about 900 branches.
markets: Millions of customers in Turkey through a branch network; small overseas presence only.
rationale: Well-known Turkish bank and volleyball sponsor, but its market is mainly domestic, limiting F1's value.

name: Aditya Birla Capital
desc: Financial services arm of the Aditya Birla Group offering lending, asset management, insurance, housing finance and wealth management in India.
markets: Retail and corporate customers across India; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Strong Indian brand within a group that sponsors sports, but customers are domestic, limiting F1 value.

name: AmeriGas
desc: Distributes propane for home heating, cooking, commercial and industrial use and operates propane cylinder exchange across the US.
markets: Residential, commercial and agricultural customers across the United States.
rationale: Commodity fuel distributor with a US-only market and no sports presence, so F1 sponsorship fits poorly.
changed: AmeriGas Partners merged into UGI in 2019

name: Ameriprise Financial
desc: Provides financial planning, wealth management, retirement, insurance and asset management through advisors and Columbia Threadneedle Investments.
markets: Affluent US retail clients and institutional investors in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Strong US brand with golf event sponsorship; F1 could reach affluent clients and suit hospitality for advisors.
changed: Spun off from American Express in 2005

name: Ant International
desc: Offers digital payments, wallet and fintech services such as Alipay+, Antom and WorldFirst connecting merchants and users across many markets.
markets: Connects merchants and users in over 100 markets, serving global brands and tourist payment flows.
rationale: Alipay+ tourist network spans many markets and Singapore hosts a Grand Prix; rival payments brands already sponsor F1.
changed: Created in 2023 as the international arm of Ant Group

name: Bajaj Finserv
desc: Indian financial services holding company with Bajaj Finance lending, Bajaj Allianz insurance and Bajaj Finserv Health.
markets: Serves very large numbers of customers across India through EMI cards, loans and insurance.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer brand but entirely domestic, so F1 offers limited commercial return.

name: Barings BDC
desc: Publicly traded business development company lending to middle-market private companies, externally managed by Barings.
markets: Lends to private US middle-market companies and pays income to shareholders.
rationale: Closed-end lending vehicle with no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship makes no commercial sense.

name: Goldman Sachs BDC
desc: Publicly traded business development company lending to US middle-market companies through senior secured loans, managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management.
markets: Lends to US middle-market companies and pays income to institutional and retail shareholders.
rationale: Financial product with no consumer visibility; any F1 interest would sit with Goldman Sachs, not this vehicle.
f1: Managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management; Goldman Sachs is a current Formula 1 partner.

name: Great-West Lifeco
desc: Financial holding company owning Canada Life, Empower and Irish Life, offering life and health insurance, retirement plans and wealth management.
industry: life insurance and retirement holding company
markets: Customers in Canada, the United States and Europe through Canada Life, Empower and Irish Life.
rationale: Known in Canada and Europe through brands that have sponsored sports; F1 could support Empower and Canada Life awareness.

name: Groww
desc: Indian fintech platform offering stock broking, mutual funds, futures and options trading, IPOs, loans and wealth products to retail investors.
markets: Retail investors across India, with over 12 million active clients.
rationale: Strong consumer app brand among young Indian investors with active advertising, but entirely domestic.
changed: Listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025
